stem: How did President Dwight D. Eisenhower respond to "considerable resistance" in Arkansas?

options.label: F
options.text: By sending soldiers to Arkansas to enforce desegregation

options.label: G
options.text: By closing schools in Arkansas until desegregation was achieved

options.label: H
options.text: By declaring school segregation to be a decision for the state of Arkansas to make

options.label: J
options.text: By firing public school teachers in Arkansas who supported segregation

visual_elements: Text box with excerpt: On May 17, 1954, U.S. Supreme Court Justice Earl Warren delivered the unanimous ruling in the landmark civil rights case Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, Kansas. . . . There was considerable resistance to the Supreme Court's ruling. . . . —“Brown v. Board of Education (1954),” National Archives and Records Administration, www.ourdocuments.gov (accessed February 28, 2018)
